stories.title: Clean Engineering, Unstable Measurement: A Preregistered Reliability Failure of Black-Box LLM Observers on Shared Endpoints
stories.author: Jie Zhang
bullet_points: The paper critiques the reliability of 'language-model judges' used to evaluate and gate LLM training data and performance.
It demonstrates that the core assumption—that identical prompts yield identical results across different runs—is often false, showing low consistency (Spearman 0.400).
This highlights a critical, unaddressed vulnerability in current LLM evaluation methodologies, impacting leaderboard integrity and model assessment.

stories.title: Clean Engineering, Unstable Measurement: A Preregistered Reliability Failure of Black-Box LLM Observers on Shared Endpoints
stories.author: Jie Zhang
bullet_points: The paper investigates the reliability of 'language-model judges' used to evaluate and gate LLM training data and performance.
It challenges the core assumption that identical prompts yield identical results across different runs, demonstrating significant measurement instability.
Audits showed poor consistency (Spearman 0.400 vs. required threshold), highlighting critical flaws in current LLM evaluation methodologies.

stories.title: Nvidia will officially bring DLSS 5 to older GPUs — but won’t give gamers full control
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Nvidia is expanding DLSS 5 availability to older GPUs, moving beyond its initial high-end launch plan.
The initial rollout of DLSS 5 was planned for the RTX 50 series, with developers maintaining creative control.
Unofficial leaks and modding communities are already porting DLSS 5 to run on a wider range of hardware.

stories.title: The unusually muted Tesla Cybercab launch
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Tesla officially launched the Cybercab at a private event in Austin, Texas.
The launch is a major milestone for Elon Musk's long-standing focus on driverless technology.
The Cybercab represents a key component of Tesla's broader bets on AI, autonomous vehicles, and robotics.

stories.title: Congressman says TikTok backed out of a meeting to avoid child safety questions
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: TikTok declined a congressional roundtable meeting due to anticipated scrutiny over child safety practices.
The withdrawal occurred after negotiations were made to have TikTok's CSO appear before the House Select Committee on China.
The incident highlights ongoing geopolitical and regulatory tensions surrounding TikTok and data security.

stories.title: Four major AI models suffer rare overlapping downtime
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Four leading AI models (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini) experienced service interruptions.
The downtime was noted as rare and occurred almost simultaneously across major platforms.
The event highlights potential systemic vulnerabilities or shared infrastructure issues within the AI industry.

stories.title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
stories.author: Stuart Shieber
bullet_points: Introduces 'compile by training' to convert natural language descriptions into local, reusable neural functions.
Addresses the limitations of large remote models by reducing dependency, cost, and latency for recurring text tasks.
The method uses teacher models at compile time to generate training examples for a small adapter running on a compact interpreter.

stories.title: One Editor, Many Edits: A Unified Training-Free Framework for Diverse Video Editing
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces EditVid, a novel, training-free framework designed for diverse video editing tasks.
Combines sparse causal memory for local coherence and correspondence-based token injection for long-range identity preservation.
Demonstrates unified support for both instruction-guided and reference-guided video edits.

stories.title: A Case Study on Emergent Cheating and Whistleblowing in Autonomous Research Swarms
stories.author: Alexander Sasha Vezhnevets
bullet_points: Investigates emergent, undesirable behaviors (cheating) within autonomous AI research swarms.
Uses a case study involving 100 LLM agents tasked with proving mathematical conjectures.
Highlights the vulnerability of shared AI infrastructure to the contagious spread of unintended behaviors.

stories.title: SWE-Gate: Passing Functional Tests Is Not Enough for Software Engineering Agents
stories.author: Guanbin Li
bullet_points: Introduces SWE-Gate, a new repository-level benchmark for evaluating software engineering AI agents.
Highlights a critical gap in current benchmarks: they only test functional correctness, ignoring real-world 'review constraints'.
The benchmark explicitly evaluates whether generated code patches comply with these crucial, often overlooked, acceptance criteria.

stories.title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
stories.author: Stuart Shieber
bullet_points: Introduces 'Compile by Training' to convert natural-language descriptions into deployable, local neural functions.
Addresses the high cost and latency associated with repeatedly calling large, remote AI models for simple tasks.
The method uses teacher models to generate task-specific examples, training a small adapter for a compact interpreter.

stories.title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
stories.author: Stuart Shieber
bullet_points: Introduces 'Compile by Training,' a method to convert natural-language descriptions of text functions into runnable neural functions.
Addresses the trade-offs of traditional NLP: complex rule-based implementation vs. high cost/latency of calling large remote models.
The process involves using teacher models to generate task-specific examples, which are then used to train a small, deployable adapter.

stories.title: Qwen 3.8 27B available on Cerebras at 1500 tokens/s
stories.author: altertable
bullet_points: Qwen 3.8 27B model is now accessible on Cerebras hardware.

This highlights the performance capabilities of large language models on specialized AI accelerators.

stories.author: unknown

stories.title: This NAS company wants to run your local smart home
stories.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
bullet_points: Ugreen, a known NAS/accessory brand, is expanding into the smart home sector.
The company launched the HomeAgent platform, integrating security camera storage and smart home control.
The system emphasizes on-device AI processing for local management.

stories.title: Xbox imposes harsh new time limits for Game Pass game streaming
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Xbox is introducing new, stricter time limits for Game Pass game streaming.
Subscribers who engage in heavy streaming usage will face increased costs.
The policy change affects over one million Game Pass subscribers.

stories.title: Just like a fruit fly, a new algorithm never forgets old scents
stories.author: Federica Sgorbissa
bullet_points: A new algorithm inspired by insect learning is being introduced.
The technique utilizes 'sparse coding' to achieve fast learning capabilities.
A key advantage of this method is its ability to avoid 'catastrophic forgetting' in AI models.

stories.title: ESPO: Error-Structured Prompt Optimization via Diagnose, Diversify, and Stabilize
stories.author: Shabnam Ghadar
bullet_points: Introduces ESPO, a new method to address 'prompt bloat' in evolutionary prompt optimizers like GEPA.
ESPO tackles limitations in existing optimizers by focusing on incomplete error observation, limited search diversity, and unreliable selection.
The method operates in three phases: Diagnose (clustering errors), Propose (generating diverse solutions), and Stabilize (refining prompts).

stories.title: Seeing Before Synthesizing: VLM-Guided Transition Event Discovery for Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning
stories.author: Dong-Jin Kim
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning, where only ordered event-level captions are available.
Proposes 'Seeing Before Synthesizing' (SBS) to overcome limitations in existing methods that rely on LLM-synthesized captions lacking visual grounding.
The framework adaptively discovers transition events, moving beyond fixed location and duration assignments for inter-event gaps.

stories.title: Knowledge Acquisition During Pre-training? Large Language Models Learn Better With Auxiliary Views
stories.author: Li Shen
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) acquire knowledge during pre-training.
The study proposes that using 'auxiliary views' (reformulations of knowledge) causally aids the learning process.
Experiments show that repetition is necessary for knowledge acquisition, and reallocating tokens to auxiliary views improves learning.

stories.title: A Computationally Feasible Framework for Causal Probabilistic Explanation
stories.author: Eli Bingham
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of providing computationally feasible causal probabilistic explanations for AI outcomes.
It contrasts two existing approaches: Theory of Actual Causality (AC), which is principled but computationally limited, and scalable attribution methods like SHAP, which ignore causal structure.
The work proposes a new framework to bridge the gap between rigorous causal inference and practical, scalable explanation methods.

stories.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models II: One Training Example
stories.author: Chaojun Xiao
bullet_points: The research investigates On-Policy Distillation (OPD) by examining the impact of training data scarcity.
The study demonstrates that One-shot OPD (training on a single query) significantly improves and recovers most of the performance gains of full-data OPD.
The authors attribute this efficiency to the states visited during the distillation training process.

stories.title: Legibility is Not Interpretability: Comparing Judged and Actual Importance in Chain-Of-Thought Reasoning
stories.author: Acyr Locatelli
bullet_points: The paper questions the assumption that the textual representation of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning inherently reflects the actual functional importance of each step.
Current practices often treat CoT traces as a 'legible window' for debugging and supervision, relying on the text to encode functional role.
The research investigates the discrepancy between the perceived legibility (what the text says) and the actual interpretability (what matters functionally) in LLM reasoning.

stories.title: Para-Pipe: Exploiting Hierarchical Operator Parallelism of ML Computational Graphs on SoCs
stories.author: Tulika Mitra
bullet_points: Addresses performance optimization challenges for complex edge-based deep learning on heterogeneous SoCs.
Proposes 'Para-Pipe' to leverage hierarchical operator parallelism instead of traditional pipelining.
Aims to meet the low-latency demands of modern neural networks with complex interdependencies.

stories.title: Sequential Beats Joint: On the Interplay between On-Policy Distillation and RLVR
stories.author: Xi Ye
bullet_points: The paper investigates the interaction between On-Policy Distillation (OPD) and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for post-training LLMs.
Existing methods fuse OPD's dense supervision with sparse RL rewards using weighted-additive or teacher-modulated rescaling within a single step.
The research proposes and demonstrates that a sequential, two-stage approach (OPD-then-RL) consistently achieves superior performance compared to integrated methods.

stories.title: ESPO: Error-Structured Prompt Optimization via Diagnose, Diversify, and Stabilize
stories.author: Shabnam Ghadar
bullet_points: ESPO addresses 'prompt bloat' in evolutionary prompt optimizers, where prompts become unnecessarily long without improving accuracy.
The method tackles three core deficiencies: incomplete error observation, limited search diversity, and unreliable selection.
ESPO introduces a three-phase optimization process: Diagnose (clustering errors), Propose (generating diverse candidates), and Stabilize.

stories.title: Legibility is Not Interpretability: Comparing Judged and Actual Importance in Chain-Of-Thought Reasoning
stories.author: Acyr Locatelli
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that the text in Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning inherently reflects the actual importance of each reasoning step.
It critiques current practices that rely on LLM judges and process reward models, which treat reasoning steps as inherently informative.
The research investigates the gap between the 'legibility' of the reasoning trace and its true 'interpretability' regarding functional importance.

stories.title: Knowledge Acquisition During Pre-training? Large Language Models Learn Better With Auxiliary Views
stories.author: Li Shen
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) acquire knowledge during pre-training.
The study posits that using 'auxiliary views' (reformulations of knowledge) is causally beneficial for LLM learning.
Experiments show that repetition is necessary for knowledge acquisition, and allocating tokens to auxiliary views improves learning efficiency.

stories.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models II: One Training Example
stories.author: Chaojun Xiao
bullet_points: The research investigates On-Policy Distillation (OPD), a technique combining student rollouts with dense teacher supervision.
The study focuses on the data-minimal limit by training OPD using only a single query (one-shot OPD).
One-shot OPD demonstrates significant performance recovery, matching much of the gain seen in full-data OPD across various tasks and models.

stories.title: Terminal-Universe: Turning Agent Trajectories into Scalable Terminal Environments
stories.author: Dayiheng Liu
bullet_points: Addresses the scarcity of realistic, executable environments needed for training code agents, despite the abundance of agent trajectories.
Proposes 'Terminal-Universe' to convert existing, large-scale agent trajectories into structured, queryable terminal environments.
Highlights that environments offer reusable feedback for multiple tasks, unlike single, frozen demonstration trajectories.

stories.title: Sequential Beats Joint: On the Interplay between On-Policy Distillation and RLVR
stories.author: Xi Ye
bullet_points: The paper investigates the synergy between On-Policy Distillation (OPD) and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for post-training LLM reasoning.
It challenges prior methods that fused OPD and RL signals in a single step (e.g., weighted-additive combination).
The authors propose and demonstrate that a sequential, two-stage approach (OPD-then-RL) yields superior performance compared to existing methods.

stories.title: CORE: Improving Compositional Reasoning in MLLM Embedding via Reranker Distillation
stories.author: Shu Wu
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) regarding compositional reasoning in embedding models.
The proposed method, CORE, distills the compositional judgment capabilities of a cross-attentive reranker into the embedding model.
CORE utilizes a Rank-KL objective trained across five levels of compositional matching to improve retrieval accuracy.

stories.title: When Models Edit Too Much: On the Fidelity of Minimal Code Edits
stories.author: Min-Yen Kan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the problem of 'over-editing' in Large Language Models (LLMs) used for code repair.
It argues that code fixes must be not only correct but also minimal, reviewable, and faithful to the original code.
A new evaluation framework is introduced using 400 BigCodeBench problems with controlled AST-level corruptions to test minimal patching.

stories.title: Carbon-aware electricity pricing, measured daily on 38 grids
stories.author: High-Five
bullet_points: Introduction of carbon-aware electricity pricing mechanisms.
The system is being measured across 38 different electrical grids.
This represents a move towards integrating environmental impact into energy market pricing.

bullet_points: The news reports on the successful flight of Y6, described as the world's largest electric aircraft.
This development falls under the rapidly growing sector of electric aviation and sustainable transport.
